input.quote: 13. NON-SOLICITATION OF EMPLOYEES. Neither party shall, during the term of this Agreement and for one (1) year after its termination, solicit for hire as an employee, consultant or otherwise any of the other party's personnel who have had direct involvement with the Services, without such other party's express written consent, which shall not be unreasonably withheld.
input.rationale: Section 13 is the only non-solicit in the agreement and it binds us as well as Contractor. It already satisfies two fallback elements (mutual, and limited to personnel with direct involvement in the Services) and is a solicitation restriction only, not a no-hire. It fails the fallback on duration and carve-outs: the restriction runs for the whole term plus one year after termination, so for personnel whose involvement ended early it can bite far longer than 12 months from the end of their involvement (and potentially beyond 24 months); and there is no exclusion for general advertisements or unsolicited approaches. Our redline makes the shortest conforming edits — re-anchoring the period to twelve months from the end of the individual's involvement and adding the two carve-outs — leaving the consent mechanic and the rest of the clause untouched.

mappings.element: The restriction covers only personnel directly involved in the Services.

proposal.summary: Narrow mutual non-solicit to 12 months from end of involvement and add general-advertising / unsolicited-approach carve-outs
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We can accept a mutual non-solicit, but only for twelve months measured from the end of the individual's involvement in the Services rather than the term plus a year, and it must carve out general advertisements and unsolicited approaches.
